title: Assam BJP launches Jan Jagaran processions against Congress over SIR

tea.why: Protesting against Congress party opposition to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and alleged attempts to undermine democracy.
tea.want: To awaken public awareness against opposition activities and reaffirm support for constitutional institutions and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
tea.changed: Oct 13: Assam BJP launched statewide Jan Jagaran processions and rallies spanning until October 31.

summary: The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party in Assam initiated statewide Jan Jagaran processions and peaceful mass rallies across district headquarters, starting from October 13 until October 31, 2026. Organised by the BJP, the campaign aims to oppose the Congress party's resistance to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and alleged efforts to blackmail constitutional bodies and shield illegal immigrants. According to state leaders including Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and state BJP president Dilip Saikia, the demonstrations seek to defend the independence of constitutional institutions, support Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision, and counter what they described as politically motivated anarchy.
demands: Preserve the independence of constitutional institutions
Oppose opposition tactics against the Special Intensive Revision
response: Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and state BJP leaders announced and led the political campaign to counter opposition marches and support constitutional bodies.

updates.text: Assam BJP announced and commenced statewide Jan Jagaran processions and rallies running through October 31.
